name: IN-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 21 points in partisan baseline
Incumbent André Carson is running with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Carson's win chances near 97%
Republican challenger has no reported fundraising or polling support
model.rationale: Indianapolis-based IN-07 is heavily Democratic, and Carson is a well-funded incumbent facing a challenger with no visible financial or polling footprint. Markets price this near-certain for Carson, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise wave-level Republican environment or a late Carson scandal could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
André Carson, a Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in this Indianapolis-based district that leans about 21 points Democratic. He has raised over a million dollars and holds more than $600,000 on hand, while Republican Patrick McAuley has no reported fundraising and Libertarian James Sceniak is also on the ballot. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Carson's win probability around 97%, and the district's fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit margin. The race is rated Safe D, with the main uncertainty being how large the final margin will be rather than who wins.
